name: Ketamine
executiveSummary: Dissociative anesthesia / analgesia. IV induction **1–2 mg/kg** (IM **5 mg/kg**). Analgesia **0.1–0.5 mg/kg** bolus or **0.12–0.36 mg/kg/h**. Sedation infusion **0.25–2 mg/kg/h**. NICU: **0.5–2 mg/kg** IV / **0.5–1 mg/kg/h** — specialist.
indications:
## Indications

- Brief induction/anesthesia; procedural analgesia; selected ICU sedation.
- Intubation: **2–3 mg/kg** IV in pediatric regimens.

## Precautions

- ↑ BP/HR; sialorrhea; dreams/hallucinations. Caution with ICH, open globe injury, PHT.
- Precipitates with diazepam in the same line.

> Dilute to **1–10 mg/mL** for infusion (NS/D5W).

adulto.dose: Analgesia: **0.1–0.3 mg/kg** bolus or **0.12–0.36 mg/kg/h**. Induction: **1–2 mg/kg IV**.
adulto.administration: Slow IV or infusion; dilute for drip.

pediatrico.finalConcentration: Bolus up to 50 mg/mL; usual infusion **1–2 mg/mL** (orient. max 10 mg/mL).
pediatrico.dose: IV induction **1–2 mg/kg**; IM **5 mg/kg**. Infusion **0.25–2 mg/kg/h**. Analgesia **0.5–1 mg/kg**. Intubation **2–3 mg/kg**.
pediatrico.notes: Relative contraindications: ICH, ocular trauma, PHT.

neonatal.dose: Analgesia/sedation: bolus **0.5–2 mg/kg IV** slow; infusion **0.5–1 mg/kg/h** titrated — neonatology/anesthesia only.

stability:
## Stability

- Dilution: follow local guide (often days refrigerated per pharmacy). Strict asepsis.
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Hypertension, tachycardia, sialorrhea, nystagmus, hallucinations, rare laryngospasm, ↑ ICP.
